title: Sales Enablement Playbook: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Deck Guidance, Pricing, Case Studies, Security FAQ
author: Jordan Lee
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook bundles recommended positioning and messaging, short competitive briefs, pitch-deck talking points, pricing guidance, representative TCO examples, two concise customer case studies, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this as the canonical sales-ready reference for AE/SDR/solutions engineers engaging prospects evaluating inference platforms.

How to use this doc:
- Sales: quick talking points, objection-handling bullets, and pitch-deck pages.
- Solutions Engineers: architecture guidance, competitive differentiators, benchmarks to cite.
- Product/SWEs: ensure claims map to product pages and performance benchmarks (link checklist in Related Pages).

1) Core positioning and messaging (elevator + pillars)

Elevator (15–30s):
Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes LLMs predictable and economical in production—supporting hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployments with unified tooling for latency, cost, and reliability.

Three core value pillars (talk-track bullets):
- Production-first performance: predictable latency and throughput with GPU-optimized serving, smart batching, and KV caching so apps stay fast at scale.
- Cost and economics: intelligent batching, caching, and quantization recommendations reduce per-token cost and offer clear levers for trade-offs.
- Flexible deployment: same API and operational tooling across hosted, dedicated, and private (VPC/on-prem) for security and regulatory needs.

One-liner variations (use by persona):
- Engineers: "A consistent inference runtime across hosted, dedicated and private with deep observability and predictable latency SLOs."
- Platform/security: "Private deployment options with KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and enterprise SLAs."
- Product/PM: "Ship LLM features faster with fewer surprises—transparent cost controls and rollout tools."

Key proof points to cite in conversations:
- Unified API across deployment modes (no SDK changes between Hosted/Dedicated/Private).
- Built-in fallback and routing policies for graceful degradation (model variants, region fallback).
- Observability: token-level cost/latency breakdowns and per-route dashboards.
- Quantified impact: typical clients see 20–60% reduction in token spend after applying Redwood Optimize recommendations (cite case studies).

2) Competitive brief (summary + differentiation)

Primary competitors to address in mid-market/enterprise deals:
- OpenAI (hosted API focus)
- Anthropic / Claude (hosted models + safety focus)
- AWS Bedrock / SageMaker (cloud-managed endpoints)
- Cohere / Mistral (model providers / endpoints)
- Self-hosted inference stacks (Ray, Triton, custom stacks)

How Redwood differentiates (talking points by objection):
- "Why not OpenAI?": Redwood focuses on serving economics and operational control at scale. We provide dedicated capacity, private deployments with customer-managed keys, and detailed token-level cost analytics that OpenAI’s hosted product does not expose in the same way.
- "Why not AWS Bedrock / SageMaker?": Cloud vendor endpoints are general-purpose; Redwood offers a GPU-optimized runtime, kernel selection, KV caching, and integrated quality/regression tooling that reduces unit cost and simplifies rollouts across infra boundaries.
- "Why not self-host?": Self-hosting offers control but requires significant engineering (autoscaling, batching, kernel tuning, caching). Redwood provides a drop-in platform with production SLAs and operational runbooks.

Competitive quick-reference table (use in battlecards & slide 1–2):
Name | Deployment modes | Strength | Typical downside
OpenAI | Hosted | Best-in-class model research & hosted scale | Less deployment flexibility; limited private options
AWS Bedrock | Hosted | Deep cloud integrations | Less opinionated serving optimizations; more infra overhead for cost tuning
Self-host | Private/Dedicated | Full control | High ops overhead and longer time-to-market
Redwood | Hosted/Dedicated/Private | Production economics + unified runtime + enterprise controls | Newer vendor vs hyperscalers; emphasize SLA & references

3) Pitch deck structure & recommended slide-level messaging

Recommended deck flow (10–12 slides):
1. Title / TL;DR – 15s message: "Predictable, economical LLM inference for product teams."
2. Problem – high-level pain: unpredictable latency, rising token costs, fragile rollouts.
3. Why now – model proliferation, open model ecosystem, need for serving economics.
4. Product overview – three deployment modes + console & Optimize.
5. Performance & cost proof – representative numbers (example below).
6. Architecture (high-level) – serving runtime, smart routing, caching, kernel selection.
7. Security & compliance – VPC, KMS, SOC2/ISO evidence, private control plane.
8. Pricing & procurement options – hosted PAYG, Dedicated commits, Private licensing.
9. Customer stories – 2 short case studies.
10. Rollout & success plan – POC criteria and success metrics.
11. Next steps / ask – pilot timeline, commercial ask.

Pitching tips for SEs and AEs:
- Lead with economics for platform owners and with latency/UX for product owners.
- Use customer metrics where possible (p50/p95 latency, tokens/month, cost reduction percent).
- Offer a 4–6 week pilot: initial workload migration + dashboarding + cost baseline.

Representative performance & cost numbers (callouts you can cite in demos):
- Typical hosted API p95 latency for a 2k token generation on gpt-style models: 350–750ms (vary by model & region).
- For dedicated pools, customers often achieve 30–70% higher throughput vs unmanaged endpoints due to batching and kernel optimizations.
- Use case example: e-commerce search re-ranking reduced per-query CPU/GPU cost by ~40% after enabling prefix caching & recommended quantization.

4) Pricing guidance and packaging (sales-friendly)

Pricing pillars (how to position):
- Hosted (PAYG): per-token rate for generation + per-embedding unit; simple for quick adoption.
- Dedicated (reserved): monthly committed GPU capacity with discounted per-token equivalent and burst options.
- Private (enterprise): licensing + support; typically annual with onboarding professional services.
- Add-ons: extended observability retention, premium SLA, compliance packages.

Commercial negotiation levers to offer:
- Minimum committed throughput (tokens/sec or GPU hours) for a discount band.
- Onboarding credits and a 6–12 week migration window.
- Trial period for the Optimize toolkit to demonstrate cost savings.

Example price band guidance (for AE planning only – indicative):
- Hosted PAYG: $0.0025–$0.02 per 1k tokens generated (varies by model class); embeddings $0.0005–$0.004 per unit.
- Dedicated reserved: starting monthly commits equivalent to 1–4 A100-class GPU capacity; effective per-token discount 30–60% vs PAYG for steady workloads.
- Private: negotiated platform fee + support (typical three-year procurement for regulated customers).

TCO conversation model (quick script):
1. Take baseline: current monthly tokens and average latency requirements.
2. Map to hosting option: PAYG if experimental; Dedicated if sustained > X tokens/month (use rule-of-thumb: sustained high-concurrency or predictable peak > 50M tokens/month).
3. Estimate quantization/batching savings: assume 20–50% reduction on first pass; refine during POC.
4. Present net cost and time-to-market savings versus self-hosting.

5) 2 Short case studies (one mid-market, one enterprise)

Case Study A — E-commerce search & re-ranking (Mid-market)
- Customer profile: 200M monthly sessions, 3M annotated queries/month.
- Challenge: high per-query latency and growing model costs for personalization/reranking.
- Redwood solution: migrated reranking to Dedicated pool + prefix/KV caching + quantization profile (int8 where safe).
- Outcomes (90 days): 42% reduction in per-query inference cost, p95 latency improved from 920ms to 520ms, and 18% lift in add-to-cart conversion for personalized recommendations.
- Owner / reference: Solutions Eng: Priya Narayanan (internal).

Case Study B — Regulated enterprise (financial services)
- Customer profile: global FS firm, strict data residency and KMS requirements.
- Challenge: must host models in customer VPC with customer-managed keys, maintain audit trails, and limit data egress.
- Redwood solution: Private deployment with customer-managed KMS, on-prem packaging for sensitive workloads, and integration with SIEM for audit logs.
- Outcomes (6 months): successful production rollout for 3 internal apps, compliance evidence accepted by internal risk committee, 1.5x faster model iteration velocity due to standardized rollout process compared to prior in-house setup.
- Owner / reference: Enterprise AE: Miguel Santos (internal).

6) Security FAQ for prospects (concise Q&A for sales decks and RFP responses)

Q: What deployment options do you offer for sensitive data?
A: Hosted API, Dedicated (customer-isolated GPU pools), and Private (VPC or on-prem). Private deployments include a customer-managed control plane option for strict isolation.

Q: How is data protected in transit and at rest?
A: All network traffic is TLS 1.2+ encrypted in transit. Data at rest is encrypted with AES-256; for Private deployments customers may supply KMS/HSM keys (customer-managed keys supported).

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (CMK)?
A: Yes. We support KMS integration and HSM-backed key material for Private deployments. Hosted customers can opt into CMK where available (enterprise plan).

Q: What compliance certifications do you maintain?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and is ISO 27001 certified. We provide compliance packs and evidence for customer audits under NDAs.

Q: How do you handle logs and auditing?
A: Audit logs (control plane actions, deployment events, API keys usage) are available via the Console and can be streamed to customer SIEM systems. Sensitive request/response content logging is optional and can be disabled for Private deployments.

Q: How do you prevent data leakage to model weights / training data?
A: Redwood is an inference platform — we do not train customer data into our model weights. We provide controls to disable logging of request/response payloads and provide private deployment models that are isolated to the customer environment.

Q: What security testing do you perform?
A: Regular internal pentesting, annual third-party penetration tests, and a formal vulnerability disclosure program. Customers may request attestations as part of procurement.

Q: What is your incident response and breach notification policy?
A: We maintain a documented incident response plan (IRP). Customers on enterprise plans receive SLA-backed notification timelines, and Redwood follows a 72-hour initial notification window for confirmed data incidents, with follow-up remediation and post-incident report.

Q: How do you support data residency and retention controls?
A: Customers can provision Dedicated or Private regions to meet residency requirements. Retention policies are configurable per-tenant, and deletion workflows are auditable.

7) POC / Pilot checklist (engineer-friendly steps and success metrics)

Pilot recommended scope (4–8 weeks):
- Week 0–1: Kickoff & success criteria. Capture baseline traffic, latency (p50/p95), and cost per request.
- Week 1–2: Baseline integration (test key, route traffic to Hosted or Dedicated sandbox).
- Week 2–4: Apply caching, batching, and quantization recommendations from Redwood Optimize.
- Week 4–6: Run A/B test for quality/regression monitoring; validate SLA conditions.
- Week 6–8: Finalize production rollout plan, procurement, and support onboarding.

Success metrics (example):
- Reduce per-request inference cost >= 25% while keeping model quality delta <= 1% on defined evals.
- Achieve target p95 latency under agreed SLO (e.g., p95 < 800ms for 2k token responses).
- Integration readiness confirmed (dashboarding, alerting, key rotation flow).

8) Objection handling (short bullets)

Objection: "We can just self-host for lower cost."
Response: Self-hosting reduces vendor dependency but requires significant engineering investment for batching, kernel tuning and observability. Offer a detailed TCO and 6–12 week migration pilot to quantify savings.

Objection: "We need enterprise-grade compliance."
Response: Outline Private option + KMS/HSM support, SOC2/ISO evidence, and offer to run a compliance workshop with security engineering.

9) Ownership, references, and next steps

Primary owners for this playbook: Go-To-Market (Jordan Lee) and Solutions Engineering (Priya Narayanan).
For reference requests and customer references contact the AE owner listed in each case study.

Next steps for AEs/SEs:
- Use this playbook when preparing discovery calls and the 12-slide deck.
- For high-touch deals, request a security workshop with the Security & Compliance team (cc security@redwood.com).
- Track pilot KPIs in the Redwood Console and schedule a 30-day review with the customer.
